correctness.rationale: Complete finite proof: the cuboctahedron is explicitly generated as L(Q_3), with 12 vertices and 24 edges. All 495 candidate 4-sets fail edge resolution; exactly 168 of 792 5-sets resolve, proving edim=5. Both stand-alone independent implementations reproduce these totals with distinct adjacency constructions (cube-edge incidence versus Euclidean cuboctahedron) and distinct resolution predicates (unique distance signatures versus all edge-pair witness masks). Every basis incidentally covers exactly seven cube corners; 21 leave each specific corner uncovered. A slide exchanges two adjacent cube edges, so it changes cube-edge support on only one cube bipartition class; it cannot switch which bipartition class has the single uncovered corner. Complete enumeration of all 168 bases and their pairwise legal moves yields connected jump graph (948 edges, every eccentricity 5) and two 84-state slide components (360 total edges, every within-component eccentricity 6), matching the parity classes. Independent BFS implementations calculate all connected components and all 14028 jump pair distances and 6972 finite slide pair distances. A coordinate bit flip proves the two slide components are isomorphic. The vertex-metric comparison is independently exhausted (96 3-bases, connected slide graph radius 7 diameter 8). No infinite extension is claimed.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of all minimum edge-failure-localizing landmark sets and of both local/global movement geometries for the canonical cuboctahedral graph. It exposes a structural bipartition-parity obstruction forcing two equal 84-state optimal slide components, yet jump moves connect all optima. Comparing vertex-resolving landmarks on the identical graph, whose minimum slide graph is connected, isolates the mathematical source of different local mobility. Exact sizes, all-pairs shortest distances and stabilizer-orbit data are natural reusable benchmarks for fault-localization and sensor relocation; the parity invariant is a meaningful explanatory lemma rather than an arbitrary table entry. Scope is one graph and neither unproved generalization nor downstream theorem is claimed.
